lessons.subject: English
lessons.title: The passive voice
lessons.summary: Spot the passive voice and know when to use it.
lessons.curriculum: Year 6 English: use the passive voice to change how information is presented in a sentence
pages: In the active voice, the subject does the action: ‘The dog chased the ball.’
In the passive voice, the action is done to the subject: ‘The ball was chased by the dog.’
Use the passive when it does not matter who did the action: ‘The window was broken.’ Most of the time, the active voice is clearer.

check.question: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The fish was eaten by the cat.
check.explanation: The action is done to the fish: it was eaten by the cat.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Ratio
lessons.curriculum: Year 6 maths: solve problems involving the relative sizes of 2 quantities
pages: A ratio compares 2 amounts. With 2 red beads for every 1 blue bead, the ratio of red to blue is 2:1.
To make more, multiply both parts by the same number. A ratio of 2:1 is the same as 4:2 or 6:3.
A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 1 cup of sugar. For 9 cups of flour, you need 3 cups of sugar.

check.question: A drink uses 1 part juice to 4 parts water. How much water goes with 3 parts juice?

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.title: The heart and blood
lessons.summary: Find out how your heart moves blood around your body.
lessons.curriculum: Year 6 science: the main parts of the human circulatory system, and the functions of the heart, blood vessels and blood
pages: Your heart is a muscle. It pumps blood around your body all the time, even when you sleep.
Blood travels in tubes called blood vessels. Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry blood back to it.
Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to every part of your body. It also carries waste, like carbon dioxide, away.

check.question: What does the heart do?
options: It pumps blood around the body
check.explanation: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body.

lessons.subject: Computing
lessons.title: Algorithms and loops
lessons.summary: Write clear steps for a task, and repeat steps with a loop.
lessons.curriculum: Key stage 2 computing: design, write and debug programs, using sequence, selection and repetition
pages: An algorithm is a set of steps to do a task. The steps must be in the right order. This is called sequence.
A loop repeats steps. Instead of writing ‘move forward’ 4 times, you can write ‘repeat 4 times: move forward’.
Selection lets a program make a choice: ‘if it is raining, take an umbrella’. If a program goes wrong, find and fix the mistake. This is called debugging.

check.question: A robot must draw a square. Which instruction uses a loop?
options: Repeat 4 times: move forward, turn right
If there is a wall, stop
check.explanation: ‘Repeat 4 times’ is a loop: it does the same steps 4 times.
